“glucose sparing effect of fat derived fuels” (Randle et al., 1963). An alternative description is, the protein sparing effect, since
the glucose would have been made from amino acids released from protein breakdown. This well-orchestrated pattern of fuel
metabolism maintains fuels (glucose and ketones) to the brain and fatty acids and ketones to other tissues from the absorptive
period into starvation (Cahill, 2006; Watford, 2015).
